steps.run:
set +e

BASELINE=$?
ORCH1148_SIMULATE_REVERT=1 node .github/scripts/strict-grep/orch-1148-reserve-sheet-gate-mirrors-button.mjs >/dev/null 2>&1
NIGHTOUT=$?
ORCH1148_SIMULATE_VENUEID_REVERT=1 node .github/scripts/strict-grep/orch-1148-reserve-sheet-gate-mirrors-button.mjs >/dev/null 2>&1
VENUEID=$?
set -e
echo "baseline=$BASELINE isNightOut-revert=$NIGHTOUT venue_id-revert=$VENUEID"
if [ "$BASELINE" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: the gate is red on unmodified source."; exit 1
fi
if [ "$NIGHTOUT" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: re-adding isNightOut/nightOut to the SHEET gate did not fail the guard (exit $NIGHTOUT)."
  echo "      Exit 2 means the harness could not find its target — the anchors are stale and the"
  echo "      fails-on-revert proof is asserting nothing. Re-point it; do not delete it."
  exit 1
fi
if [ "$VENUEID" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: removing venue_id from the BUTTON gate did not fail the guard (exit $VENUEID)."
  echo "      That is the #1605 P0-1 dead tap, and it is the regression this guard missed once."
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: the guard is green on HEAD and red on both documented reverts."

steps.name: postgres-17-runtime: Provision GoTrue-managed auth.users columns (privileged)
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
DDL="ALTER TABLE auth.users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS phone text;"

# `supabase_admin` is the image's bootstrap SUPERUSER and its password
# is the same POSTGRES_PASSWORD this job already uses, so the DDL runs
# over the ordinary TCP connection — no `docker exec`, no dependence
# on `docker ps --filter ancestor`, and no dependence on an OS user
# inside the container.
#
# TESTER NOTE (#1529): the original form of this step shelled into the
# container and tried `psql -U supabase_admin` over the LOCAL SOCKET
# with no password. That fails on the stock image — pg_hba grants
# `trust` for local/127.0.0.1 but the connection still prompts
# ("fe_sendauth: no password supplied"), and the one route that does
# connect (`-U postgres`) is not the owner of auth.users, so its ALTER
# is refused. All three routes failed, `provisioned` stayed 0, and the
# step exited 1 BEFORE migrations were applied — which would have
# aborted postgres-17-runtime at step 1 of 6 and made the five SQL
# steps unreachable. Verified against supabase/postgres:17.4.1.075.
psql -h localhost -U supabase_admin -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 \
  -c "$DDL"

# Verify through the UNPRIVILEGED connection the tests actually use.
# This is the assertion that matters: provisioning the tests cannot
# see is not provisioning.
psql -h localhost -U postgres -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -Atc \
  "select 1 from information_schema.columns
    where table_schema='auth' and table_name='users'
      and column_name='phone'" | grep -qx 1
echo "auth.users.phone is visible to the test connection"

DDL="ALTER TABLE auth.users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS phone text;"

# `supabase_admin` is the image's bootstrap SUPERUSER and its password
# is the same POSTGRES_PASSWORD this job already uses, so the DDL runs
# over the ordinary TCP connection — no `docker exec`, no dependence
# on `docker ps --filter ancestor`, and no dependence on an OS user
# inside the container.
#
# TESTER NOTE (#1529): the original form of this step shelled into the
# container and tried `psql -U supabase_admin` over the LOCAL SOCKET
# with no password. That fails on the stock image — pg_hba grants
# `trust` for local/127.0.0.1 but the connection still prompts
# ("fe_sendauth: no password supplied"), and the one route that does
# connect (`-U postgres`) is not the owner of auth.users, so its ALTER
# is refused. All three routes failed, `provisioned` stayed 0, and the
# step exited 1 BEFORE migrations were applied — which would have
# aborted postgres-17-runtime at step 1 of 6 and made the five SQL
# steps unreachable. Verified against supabase/postgres:17.4.1.075.
psql -h localhost -U supabase_admin -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 \
  -c "$DDL"

# Verify through the UNPRIVILEGED connection the tests actually use.
# This is the assertion that matters: provisioning the tests cannot
# see is not provisioning.
psql -h localhost -U postgres -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -Atc \
  "select 1 from information_schema.columns
    where table_schema='auth' and table_name='users'
      and column_name='phone'" | grep -qx 1
echo "auth.users.phone is visible to the test connection"

templateReplay.name: postgres-replay: SC-47 baseline capture (pre-#1931)
templateReplay.run:
set -euo pipefail
for f in $(find supabase/migrations -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.sql' | sort); do
  case "$f" in
    *_issue_1931_*) continue ;;
    # issue #2160 — SKIPPED FOR THE SAME REASON #1931 IS.
    #
    # This phase deliberately runs the chain WITHOUT #1931, and #2160
    # re-emits `pg_direct_event_checkout_bundle`, whose CURRENT body
    # (defined by #1931 itself) calls
    # `issue_1931_event_ordinary_read_blocked`. A `LANGUAGE sql` body
    # is validated at CREATE time, so applying #2160 here aborts with
    # "function public.issue_1931_event_ordinary_read_blocked(uuid)
    # does not exist". The reference is CORRECT — it is the private-
    # event guard on a public reader — and removing it to satisfy this
    # lane would be deleting a security control to make CI green.
    #
    # Skipping is the same remedy this lane already applies to #1931,
    # and #2160 is covered end-to-end by its own lane, which replays
    # the FULL chain in true order and runs seven executable suites
    # twice. Any future migration that re-emits a #1931-defined object
    # belongs on this list too.
    *_issue_2160_*) continue ;;
    # issue #2333 — SKIPPED ON THE SAME GROUND, per the standing
    # instruction three lines above ("any future migration that
    # re-emits a #1931-defined object belongs on this list too").
    #
    # 20270427002335 re-emits `pg_discover_business_events` to add the
    # online carve-out. That function's CURRENT body — defined by #1931
    # itself — calls `issue_1931_event_ordinary_read_blocked`, and a
    # `LANGUAGE sql` body is validated at CREATE time, so applying it in
    # this deliberately-pre-#1931 chain aborts with "function
    # public.issue_1931_event_ordinary_read_blocked(uuid) does not exist".
    # The reference is CORRECT — it is the private-event guard on a public
    # reader — and stripping it to green this lane would delete a security
    # control. #2333's own lane replays the FULL chain in true order.
    #
    # Only ...002335 is listed: ...002333 and ...002334 re-emit plpgsql
    # bodies, which are NOT validated at CREATE time, so they replay clean.
    *_issue_2333_discover_online_carveout*) continue ;;
    # issue #2462 — SKIPPED under the standing instruction above.
    #
    # 20270522002462 re-emits `pg_direct_event_checkout_bundle`, the
    # function #1931 itself defines (...001931...:974). That body is
    # `LANGUAGE sql`, validated at CREATE time, and it carries
    # `AND NOT public.issue_1931_event_ordinary_read_blocked(e.id)`.
    # The call is CORRECT — it is the private-event deny on a public
    # reader — and removing it to green this lane would delete a
    # security control.
    #
    # It ALSO reads `e.multi_date_pricing_mode`, a column added only
    # by the skipped #2160. PostgreSQL resolves column names before
    # function signatures, so the column error is reported FIRST and
    # masks the guard error; fixing the column alone still aborts on
    # the missing function. Both faults are real and the re-emission
    # governs.
    #
    # #2462 has NO dedicated lane. It is proven end-to-end by the 3
    # unfiltered full-chain lanes that trigger on
    # `supabase/migrations/**` — the `migration-chain` job of
    # `postgres-contract-suites.yml`, the SECURITY DEFINER anon-grant
    # gate and Supabase Migrations + Stripe Deno — plus #2462's own
    # in-migration `DO $probe$` and two mingla-business jest suites.
    #
    # The count fell from ten to three at #2591, which collapsed eight
    # of the original ten into `migration-chain`. That job replays
    # every migration from zero, unconditionally and with no `if:` on
    # the replay mode, so the property those eight supplied is
    # preserved once rather than eight times. On #2462's own PR head
    # all ten predecessors ran `success`; the evidence is unchanged,
    # its provider is not.
    #
    # Matched by EXACT filename, never `*_issue_2462_*`: that glob
    # would also drop ...002463_issue_2462_phone_backfill.sql, which
    # is healthy, replays clean and is deliberately NOT skipped
    # (515 files apply here; the glob would leave 514).
    #
    # `.github/scripts/strict-grep/issue-2492-replay-skip-closure.mjs`
    # now enforces this list instead of trusting the comment.
    *20270522002462_issue_2462_checkout_determinism.sql) continue ;;
    # issue #2562 — SKIPPED at the request of, and attributed to, the
    # owner of #2564, who traced the mechanism and approved the entry.
    #
    # This is an OVERLOAD SPLIT, not a stale definition.
    # `issue_1930_ticket_checkout_create_session_base` was created by
    # #1930 taking 11 arguments. #2160 added a 12th
    # (`p_event_date_ids uuid[] DEFAULT NULL`), and both #2462 and #2562
    # carry that 12-argument shape. This lane skips `*_issue_2160_*`, so
    # when #2562 runs here its `CREATE OR REPLACE` replaces NOTHING: the
    # argument list does not match, so PostgreSQL ADDS A SECOND FUNCTION.
    # `pg_proc` then holds two rows under that name — the guardless
    # 11-argument original and the 12-argument one carrying the guard.
    #
    # #2562's probe reads `pg_get_functiondef` with no signature filter,
    # and `SELECT ... INTO` in plpgsql takes the first row of an
    # unordered scan, so it inspects the 11-argument one. Its error is
    # literally true of the function it looked at.
    #
    # So the skip is NECESSARY, not convenient: on this lane the
    # migration leaves a guardless overload installed, and a delta that
    # re-emits #2462's body cannot mean anything on a chain built
    # without #2160 or #2462. The replay is incoherent here, not merely
    # strict.
    #
    # Coverage is NOT lost. #2562 lives under `supabase/migrations/**`,
    # so the 10 unfiltered full-chain lanes replay it WITH #2160 and
    # #2462 present — the only configuration in which the probe's
    # precondition holds. Same coverage argument recorded for #2462
    # directly above.
    #
    # Matched by EXACT filename, never an issue-number infix.
    *20270525002562_issue_2562_past_event_guard.sql) continue ;;
    # issue #2696 — SKIPPED because this deliberately pre-#1931 lane
    # also skips #2160. Without #2160's 11-to-12-argument transition,
    # the 11-argument `biz_ticket_checkout_create_session` wrapper
    # survives and #2696's 12-argument `CREATE OR REPLACE` creates a
    # second overload instead of replacing it. #2696's name-only
    # probe then reads the unscoped survivor and correctly aborts.
    #
    # The probe and its `AND event_id=p_event_id` conjunct are correct
    # and remain untouched. The unfiltered canonical migration replay
    # is the execution authority for #2696 in true filename order.
    # Matched by EXACT filename, never an issue-number infix.
    *20270601002696_issue_2696_event_scoped_session_lookup.sql) continue ;;
    *20270607002774_issue_2774_public_hero_alt.sql) continue ;;
    # issue #2491 C2 steps 3+4 — SKIPPED FOR THE SAME REASON #2160 IS.
    #
    # This phase deliberately runs the chain WITHOUT #1931, and #2491
    # re-emits `pg_direct_event_checkout_bundle` to switch its sold
    # subquery onto `ticket_types.sold_count`. That function's CURRENT
    # body — defined by #1931 — calls
    # `issue_1931_event_ordinary_read_blocked` and reads
    # `multi_date_pricing_mode`, and a `LANGUAGE sql` body is validated
    # at CREATE time, so applying #2491 here aborts.
    #
    # Listed by EXACT FILENAME, never by an `*_issue_2491_*` infix: the
    # infix would also swallow the step-1 counter migration and the
    # step-1b observer, which this phase must still apply.
    *20270604002491_issue_2491_c2_step34_switch_sold_readers.sql) continue ;;
    # issue #2879 — SKIPPED FOR THE SAME REASON #2491's step 3/4 is.
    # This phase replays the chain WITHOUT #1931, and #2879 re-emits
    # `pg_direct_event_checkout_bundle` to make the payment-redirect
    # window count as held. That function's body reaches
    # `issue_1931_event_ordinary_read_blocked` and
    # `multi_date_pricing_mode`, validated at CREATE time.
    # EXACT FILENAME: an `*_issue_2879_*` infix would swallow every
    # later migration of this umbrella too.
    *20270609002879_issue_2879_redirect_window_counts_as_held.sql) continue ;;
    # issue #2489 — SKIPPED under the standing instruction above ("any
    # future migration that re-emits a #1931-defined object belongs on
    # this list too").
    #
    # 20270523002489 re-emits `pg_direct_event_checkout_bundle` and
    # `pg_public_event_by_slug`, both defined by #1931 itself, to move an
    # address-privacy fallback inside the privacy gate. Both bodies are
    # `LANGUAGE sql`, validated at CREATE time, and both carry
    # `AND NOT public.issue_1931_event_ordinary_read_blocked(e.id)`.
    # It also re-emits `pg_discover_business_events`, which carries the
    # same deny.
    #
    # The deny is CORRECT — it is the private-event guard on a public
    # reader — and stripping it to green this deliberately-pre-#1931
    # chain would delete a security control to satisfy CI, which is the
    # exact defect class #2489 exists to close. The re-emission also
    # reads `e.multi_date_pricing_mode`, a column supplied only by the
    # already-skipped #2160, so this migration would abort here on two
    # independent faults even if the deny were removed.
    #
    # Covered end-to-end by the unfiltered full-chain lanes that trigger
    # on `supabase/migrations/**`, which replay every migration in true
    # filename order and run both #2489 fixtures against the terminal
    # state — the state a filtered lane structurally cannot observe.
    #
    # Matched by EXACT filename, never `*_issue_2489_*`, for the same
    # reason recorded for #2462 directly above.
    *20270523002489_issue_2489_address_privacy_server_gate.sql) continue ;;
    # #2489 PHASE 2 — the base-relation grant change. Skipped here for a
    # reason that is a consequence of the line directly above, not a
    # separate judgement.
    #
    # Phase 2 does two things this lane cannot host together. It removes
    # `anon`'s table-level SELECT on `public.events` and grants back a
    # column subset; and it gives `events_public_view` OWNER rights,
    # which is what keeps that view readable once the base grant narrows

    #
    # On this lane the gated, owner-rights definition of that view is

    #
    # The skip is NOT a way to green the lane by dropping a control:

    #
    # Matched by EXACT filename, never `*_issue_2489_*`, for the same

    *20270528002489_issue_2489_phase2_base_relation_grant.sql) continue ;;

templateReplay.name: postgres-replay: Canonical migration replay — phase 1 (chain except #2117)
templateReplay.run:
set -euo pipefail
for f in $(find supabase/migrations -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.sql' | sort); do
  case "$f" in
    *20270415002117_issue_2117_offering_visibility_gate.sql) continue ;;
    # issue #2489 — SKIPPED for the same reason this phase skips #2117.
    #
    # This phase deliberately runs the chain WITHOUT #2117, and
    # 20270523002489 re-emits `pg_public_experience_by_slug`, whose
    # CURRENT body — defined by #2117 itself — calls
    # `pg_offering_visibility_gate`. A `LANGUAGE sql` body is validated
    # at CREATE time, so applying #2489 here aborts with "function
    # public.pg_offering_visibility_gate(...) does not exist".
    #
    # The reference is CORRECT — it is the visibility control on a public
    # reader — and removing it to green this lane would delete that
    # control. #2489 re-emits the function only to route its
    # address-privacy predicate through the one shared definition; the
    # visibility arm is untouched.
    #
    # Covered end-to-end by the unfiltered full-chain lanes that trigger
    # on `supabase/migrations/**`, which replay the FULL chain in true
    # filename order.
    #
    # Matched by EXACT filename, never an issue-number infix.
    *20270523002489_issue_2489_address_privacy_server_gate.sql) continue ;;
    # issue #2728 -- the fix-forward definition must not land before
    # the pre-#2117 baseline; doing so contaminates the before-state.
    *20270605002728_issue_2728_ticket_sold_count_namespace.sql) continue ;;
    *20270607002774_issue_2774_public_hero_alt.sql) continue ;;
    # issue #3801 — SKIPPED for the same reason as the line above. It
    # re-emits `pg_public_trip_by_slug` (the packages come back in the
    # order the host authored), whose CURRENT body — defined by #2117
    # itself — calls `pg_offering_visibility_gate`, which this phase
    # does not have. A `LANGUAGE sql` body is validated at CREATE time.
    # The visibility arm is untouched. Covered by the unfiltered
    # full-chain lanes, which replay it in true filename order and run
    # its own suite. EXACT FILENAME, never an issue-number infix.
    *20270830003801_issue_3801_public_trip_tiers_ordered.sql) continue ;;
    *20271015003859_issue_3859_installment_capability_refusal.sql) continue ;;
    *20271018003859_issue_3859_public_installment_capability.sql) continue ;;
    # issue #2491 C2 steps 3+4 — SKIPPED for the same reason this phase
    # skips #2117. #2491 re-emits `pg_direct_event_checkout_bundle`,
    # whose CURRENT body reaches `issue_2489_address_withheld` /
    # `issue_2489_public_theme`, which this phase does not have.
    # EXACT FILENAME: an `*_issue_2491_*` infix would also skip the
    # step-1 and step-1b migrations, which this phase must apply.
    *20270604002491_issue_2491_c2_step34_switch_sold_readers.sql) continue ;;
    # issue #2879 — same reason: the re-emitted bundle reaches
    # `issue_2489_address_withheld` / `issue_2489_public_theme`,
    # which this phase does not have. EXACT FILENAME.
    *20270609002879_issue_2879_redirect_window_counts_as_held.sql) continue ;;
    # issue #3313 — same reason: it re-emits the bundle, whose body
    # reaches `issue_2489_address_withheld` / `issue_2489_public_theme`,
    # which this phase does not have. EXACT FILENAME.
    *20270702003313_issue_3313_recurring_event_occurrences.sql) continue ;;
    # issue #2986 — this additive resolver delegates to #2117's
    # visibility authority. It is applied exactly once after phase 2.
    *20270614002986_issue_2986_public_search_documents.sql) continue ;;
    # issue #3176 — the IndexNow outbox trigger targets #2986's
    # `public_search_documents`, which does not exist in this
    # pre-#2117 phase. The migration and its controls remain intact;
    # this filtered lane omits it by EXACT FILENAME.
    *20270627003176_issue_3176_indexnow_outbox.sql) continue ;;
    # issue #3193 — SKIPPED for the same reason as the line above. It
    # re-emits `public_search_source_facts`, one of #2986's readers,
    # and its closing DO block asserts the anonymous resolver's
    # EXECUTE grant — an object only #2986 creates, which this phase
    # has not applied yet. A DO block EXECUTES during the replay, so
    # the reference is resolved here, not deferred. Applied exactly
    # once, in its own step, straight after #2986. EXACT FILENAME,
    # never an issue-number infix.
    *20270624003193_issue_3193_public_search_live_brand_row.sql) continue ;;
    # issue #3197 — SKIPPED for the same reason as #3193. Its closing

steps.name: postgres-replay: #2353 T-20 — the apply-order guard refuses, and commits nothing
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
MIG=supabase/migrations/20270429002353_issue_2353_format_truth_and_edit_grant.sql
psql -h localhost -U postgres -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q \
  -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS issue_2353_order_guard;" \
  -c "CREATE DATABASE issue_2353_order_guard;"
set +e
OUT=$(psql -h localhost -U postgres -d issue_2353_order_guard -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f "$MIG" 2>&1)
RC=$?
set -e
echo "$OUT"
if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: 20270429002353 applied CLEANLY to a database without 20270422001972."
  echo "      S0 is inert. Applying in the wrong order would silently reverse every"
  echo "      fix in this migration with no error anywhere (#2353)."
  exit 1
fi
echo "$OUT" | grep -q 'issue_2353_requires_20270422001972_applied_first' || {
  echo "FAIL: it refused, but not with S0's own error. The operator would be shown a"
  echo "      symptom instead of the cause (#2353)."; exit 1; }
# Nothing committed: the four functions #2353 corrects must be absent,
# and so must the transitional grant.
LEFT=$(psql -h localhost -U postgres -d issue_2353_order_guard -tAc \
  "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid=p.pronamespace
    WHERE n.nspname='public' AND p.proname IN (
      'business_event_draft_payload_from_graph','business_update_live_event',
      'ari_execute_event_operation');")
if [ "$LEFT" != "0" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: the refused migration left $LEFT function(s) behind. A guard that raises"
  echo "      AFTER installing schema has already done the damage it exists to"
  echo "      prevent (#2353)."; exit 1; fi
psql -h localhost -U postgres -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q \
  -c "DROP DATABASE issue_2353_order_guard;"
echo "PASS T-20 — S0 raised issue_2353_requires_20270422001972_applied_first and"
echo "committed nothing."

steps.run:

  "SELECT p.proname, array_to_string(p.proacl,' | ') AS acl
     FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid=p.pronamespace
    WHERE n.nspname='public'
      AND p.proname IN ('business_patch_event_taxonomy','business_patch_event_when',
                        'business_update_live_event','business_update_live_event_atomic')
    ORDER BY 1;"
psql -h localhost -U postgres -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c \
  "DO \$\$
   BEGIN
     IF NOT has_function_privilege('authenticated',
          'public.business_patch_event_taxonomy(uuid,text,text[],text[],text[],numeric,numeric,text,text)','EXECUTE')
        OR NOT has_function_privilege('authenticated',
          'public.business_patch_event_when(uuid,jsonb,text,integer)','EXECUTE') THEN
       RAISE EXCEPTION 'SC-1 FAIL: authenticated cannot reach a patch leaf a shipped build still calls';
     END IF;
     IF has_function_privilege('anon',
          'public.business_patch_event_taxonomy(uuid,text,text[],text[],text[],numeric,numeric,text,text)','EXECUTE')
        OR has_function_privilege('anon',

       RAISE EXCEPTION 'SC-1 FAIL: the demoted leaf business_update_live_event is reachable by authenticated';

routing.rationale: MEASURED by tracing every gate this lane runs: its wiring gate, the auth-ready gate, the source-pin audit and the quarantine audit read mingla-business/app and mingla-business/src in full, and the typecheck delta typechecks the whole business graph, which tsconfig paths resolves into packages/. The manifest parity and ratchet-frontier steps read .github/ci-batch/MANIFEST.json and parse every workflow.
